methods.summary: Create a new [`ScanBuilder`] instance.

methods.name: with_correlation_id
methods.signature: fn with_correlation_id(self, correlation_id: impl Into<Arc<str>>) -> Self
methods.summary: Attach an opaque, caller-supplied correlation id for joining this scan's metric events to the caller's own request or operation id. An empty id is treated as unset. When unset, behavior is unchanged.

methods.name: with_partition_values
methods.summary: Configure partition value output for the scan. See [`PartitionValuesOptions`].

methods.name: with_predicate
methods.signature: fn with_predicate(self, predicate: impl Into<Option<PredicateRef>>) -> Self
methods.summary: Optionally provide an expression to filter rows. For example, using the predicate `x < 4` to return a subset of the rows in the scan which satisfy the filter. If `predicate_opt` is `None`, this is a no-op.

methods.name: with_schema
methods.summary: Provide [`Schema`] for columns to select from the [`Snapshot`].

methods.name: with_schema_opt
methods.summary: Optionally provide a [`SchemaRef`] for columns to select from the [`Snapshot`]. See [`ScanBuilder::with_schema`] for details. If `schema_opt` is `None` this is a no-op.

methods.name: with_stats
methods.summary: Configure stats output for the scan. See [`StatsOptions`].

methods.name: without_row_transforms
methods.summary: Declare that the engine will reconstruct logical rows itself and will not consume [`ScanMetadata::scan_file_transforms`].

items.name: ScanMetadata
items.summary: [`ScanMetadata`] contains (1) a batch of [`FilteredEngineData`] specifying data files to be scanned and (2) a vector of transforms (one transform per scan file) that must be applied to the data read from those files.

methods.name: visit_scan_files
methods.signature: fn visit_scan_files<T>(&self, context: T, callback: ScanCallback<T>) -> DeltaResult<T>

items.name: StatsOptions
items.summary: Engine-facing stats options. Pass to [`ScanBuilder::with_stats`] to declare what stats data the engine wants in scan metadata output. Two orthogonal axes: JSON stats (`add.stats`) and struct stats (`add.stats_parsed`).

methods.name: all
methods.summary: Both JSON and struct stats. Pays for both representations.

methods.name: all_struct
methods.summary: All struct stats, no JSON. Cheap path for engines that consume `stats_parsed` directly: avoids the per-batch `ToJson` cost on parsed-stats checkpoints.

methods.name: json_only
methods.summary: JSON only. Equivalent to [`Default::default`].

methods.name: none
methods.summary: **Disables all stats work**: no stats output, no internal data skipping (even when a predicate is set). Kernel reads no stats columns from parquet at all. Use when the engine handles its own pruning.

methods.name: struct_columns
methods.summary: Struct stats projected to the specified columns, no JSON. Like [`Self::all_struct`] but narrowed to a subset of indexed columns.
